title: Skip install prompt inside native iOS/Android apps
summary: Inside the Seed Bible phone apps (the iOS and Android app-store apps), people should never be asked to "install" Seed Bible, because they already have it. This change makes the apps count as already installed, so the install pop-up and the **Install App** entry in Settings are hidden there. The website should behave exactly as before, which is what these tests check: the change can't be tried in the phone apps from this pull request (see "Not covered").

setup.title: Use a private window in a normal browser
setup.body: Open a private/incognito window in Chrome, Edge, Safari or Firefox (Ctrl+Shift+N in Chrome/Edge, Cmd+Shift+N on Mac; Ctrl+Shift+P in Firefox). A private window acts like a first visit. Don't use a Seed Bible you've already installed to your home screen or desktop: it must be an ordinary browser tab. You don't need to sign in.

setup.title: Open the preview build
setup.body: Open the preview link at the top of this page in that private window. If it shows an error or doesn't load, the build may still be deploying: wait a few minutes and reload. If the page looks like an older version, do a hard refresh (Ctrl+Shift+R, or Cmd+Shift+R on Mac).

sections.title: The website still offers to install
sections.intro: The change should only affect the phone apps. In a browser tab, everything install-related should look the same as before.

tests.title: The install pop-up appears on the next visit after declining the tour
tests.why: Checks that a normal browser is not mistaken for the phone app, which would hide the install offer from everyone on the website.
tests.before: Use a fresh private window (close any earlier private windows first).
steps: When **Welcome to Seed Bible. Would you like a tutorial?** appears, choose **No, thanks**.
Reload the page (F5, or Cmd+R on Mac) and wait for the Bible text to appear.
expected: After the reload, a pop-up appears saying **Add Seed Bible to your desktop** (or **home screen** on a phone) **to return anytime. You can always find this option later in Settings.**
It has **Install App** and **Maybe later** buttons (on an iPhone or iPad it shows Share-button steps and **Got it** instead).

tests.title: Settings still lists Install App in a browser tab
tests.before: Same private window as the last test. If the install pop-up is open, choose **Maybe later**.
steps: Look through the list of Settings pages.
expected: There is an **Install App** entry with an install icon.

tests.title: Choosing Install App in Settings opens the install pop-up
tests.before: Settings is open, as at the end of the last test.
expected: The same install pop-up as in the first test opens (**Add Seed Bible to your …**).

sections.title: Things that should not have changed

tests.title: An installed web app still hides the install offer
tests.why: This was already the behavior for Seed Bible added to a home screen or desktop from the website; the change sits right next to that check.
tests.before: Optional: only if you already have Seed Bible installed from the website (on a home screen, or as a desktop app), or can install it from the pop-up in the earlier tests. Mark Skip otherwise.
steps: Open Seed Bible from its home screen or desktop icon (not a browser tab).
expected: There is no **Install App** entry in Settings, and no install pop-up appears.

notCovered: The change itself, inside the iOS and Android apps: this pull request doesn't touch the app projects, so no phone-app build is made for it. After it merges to develop, it reaches Google Play's Internal testing track; check there that Settings has no **Install App** entry and that no install pop-up appears after the tutorial.
The automated test added with this change checks the same thing in code: a page set up like the phone apps reports itself as installed and never offers the install pop-up.
